subject: Re: Performance SLO - Private VPC network qualification follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO - Private VPC network qualification follow-up

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the performance requirements for the Private VPC deployment: 

Summary of SLO targets you mentioned:
- 95th pct tail latency <= 120ms for streaming token responses (50 token bursts)
- Sustained throughput target: 400 concurrent streams at ~20 tokens/sec average per stream
- Peak concurrency target (burst): 600 concurrent streams for up to 10 minutes
- Internal service-to-service latency budget (app -> inference): <= 30ms

Network items to validate for qualification:
1) VPC peering / VPN path: we need the egress IPs and whether you're planning AWS Transit Gateway or direct Peering.
2) Expected egress path MTU and whether any middleboxes perform packet inspection that could add 10–50ms.
3) Whether you will permit UDP/ICMP for traceroutes and our synthetic packet tests.
4) Any rate-limited NAT gateway in front of your subnet (these can throttle concurrent streams).

Next steps I propose:
- Tom: share VPC diagram + sample network traceroute and any recent pcap if available (we can consume sanitized samples).
- Jordan (eng): we’ll run an internal network test against your staging endpoint once netops confirms peering.
- Marcus (solutions): draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and target dates.

If that looks right I’ll open a formal qualification ticket and loop in our infra team.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

--
Attachment: redwood-private-onprem-sla.pdf (product brief)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:
- The targets listed match what we need for the first phase. We can relax tail latency to 150ms for initial rollout if that helps, but will push for 120ms in steady state.
- We are planning a Transit Gateway-based architecture in AWS (us-west-2) with a dedicated VGW for Redwood peering.
- NetOps says they can provide traceroutes and a sanitized pcap, but need your guidance on which hosts to test.
- We do not currently allow ICMP from outside the VPC by default; will need to request an exception for your test window.

I'll ask NetOps to prepare the VPC diagram and a small pcap from last week. Expect that in the next 48 hours.

-Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO - Private VPC network qualification follow-up

Tom —

Perfect — thanks. A few clarifying notes for NetOps to make the tests useful:
- For traceroute: please allow UDP-based traceroute to 3 IPs we’ll provide (we use high TTL so we can measure each hop).
- For packet captures: a 2–5 minute sample of production-like traffic works — ideally during a low-traffic window. Please remove any PII.
- Target hosts: provide a staging inference endpoint (private IP or DNS) and the NAT/egress IP so we can verify path and any SNAT effects.
- If Transit Gateway has flow logs enabled, those logs are helpful (even just a 48-hr slice).

Action: Jordan, when NetOps sends the diagram/pcap, can you review for obvious jitter/MTU/fragmentation issues and propose test vectors? Also will plan a 1-hour synthetic load next week to validate 400 concurrent streams at ~20 t/s.

Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Harrington <tom.h@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO - Private VPC network qualification follow-up

Hi all —

Quick engineering notes from my side:
- Our plan for the synthetic test: ramp to 400 concurrent streaming sessions over 10 minutes, hold for 20 minutes, then spike to 600 for 10 minutes. We’ll capture per-connection RTT, token emission latency, and server-side queue times.
- Minimum requirements for your staging endpoint: TCP keepalive enabled, stable DNS resolution, and <4 packet loss for good signal.
- If you have an AWS NLB in front of the inference fleet, please confirm the idle timeout (NLB default is 350s, fine for long streams; ALBs can close earlier).
- For streaming HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 chunked: we prefer HTTP/2 for lower head-of-line; if you must use HTTP/1.1 chunked, let us know so we can adjust client concurrency.

I’ll prepare a checklist and a small test harness we can run from your staging VPC. Marcus, I’ll need the MAP template so we can lock dates.

Jordan
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
